content: BC Powder is an over-the-counter analgesic pain reliever that is owned by GlaxoSmithKline Pharmaceuticals and manufactured in Memphis, Tennessee. The name BC originates from the initials of T.C. Council, who played a role in the product's early development. Each dose of BC Powder contains 3 mg of caffeine and 195 mg of salicylamide. The product is marketed as having a faster onset of action compared to traditional pain-relief tablets due to its powdered form, which allows for quicker dissolution and absorption. BC Powder can be consumed in various ways, with the most common method being mixing it into water or soda. BC Powder is predominantly sold in the American South, where it has developed a loyal following. The brand embraces this regional popularity and actively sponsors numerous sporting events in the area. Its distinctive oval-shaped blue logo is a familiar sight at Southern minor-league baseball parks and Southeastern Conference collegiate games. Historically, BC Powder has been most commonly associated with headache relief. Many individuals, including non-users, mistakenly refer to the product as BC Headache Powder. However, recent marketing efforts by the company aim to broaden its association to include relief from general bodily aches and pains. For several years, BC Powder's television and radio advertisements have featured real-life users of the product, who are encouraged to share their personal stories through contests promoted on radio programs. A significant number of these stories have been sourced from listeners of the Charlotte, North Carolina-based radio show The Big Show with John Boy and Billy. Additionally, members of the predominantly African-American audience of the Tom Joyner Radio Show have appeared in BC Powder commercials after learning about the promotion through the program or during Joyner's annual Fantastic Voyage fantasy cruise. BC Powder also produces and markets other formulations, including BC Allergy Sinus Headache Powder and BC Arthritis Formula. The product is often confused with Goody's Powder, a similar analgesic product that contains acetaminophen instead of salicylamide. Interestingly, Goody's Powder is also owned by GlaxoSmithKline.
